member: Dr. Marcus Reid — Robotic Integration and Embedded Electronics
message:
For Dr. Amara Okafor and Prof. Kenji Tanaka, the rim slips first so the wiring must not live at the rim.

Plain words: the contact edge scrubs while the centre still sticks, so the flexible tail must leave at the nail side away from that scrub and the skin edge clamp must isolate it. I take up the Dynamics of fingertip contact during the onset of tangential slip (E67) from Dr. Elena Vasquez, which states slip starts at the periphery as an annulus around a stuck centre, which from robotic integration means the dorsal Zero Insertion Force, where Zero Insertion Force means ZIF, joint and 3.18 mm flex bend live outside the high-shear rim, so rim shear in the stick-to-slip transition vs time (E38) does not pull the connector during the 53.6 ms to 96.8 ms event.

For Dr. Elena Vasquez, finger scale and pinch force leave room for the mount.

Plain words: the fingertip stays finger sized and the pinch to hold a milk bottle is well below what the screw mount carries. The Free and Forced Vibration Modes of the Human Fingertip (E60) gives 18.0 mm width by 28.0 mm length, so our 20.0 mm by 22.0 mm body in the BioTac Product Manual (E43) is finger scale about a fingertip wide, and the required normal per finger calculation (E85) needs 9.81 N per finger to hold 1.00 kg at friction 0.500, about a milk bottle on each fingertip, well inside the 50.0 N grip rating, with 14.0 g mass in the mass budget sum (E53) about one-and-a-half teaspoons.

Ready, because mount fit, dorsal flex routing clear of rim slip, and fail-safe dual-path timing survive my strongest continuity and load objections, leaving only the named shake-plus-pull and timed-loop bench tests with Dr. Elena Vasquez.
